claim: The vast majority of the adult fly ventral nerve cord is composed of 34 hemilineages.
source: The vast majority of the adult fly ventral nerve cord is composed of 34 hemilineages, which are clusters of lineally related neurons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by the comprehensive mapping study presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hemilineages are clusters of lineally related neurons.
source: The vast majority of the adult fly ventral nerve cord is composed of 34 hemilineages, which are clusters of lineally related neurons.
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by the lineage tracing experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Neurons in hemilineages use one of three fast-acting neurotransmitters: acetylcholine, GABA, or glutamate.
source: Neurons in these hemilineages use one of the three fast-acting neurotransmitters (acetylcholine, GABA, or glutamate) for communication.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by comprehensive immunohistochemistry and genetic reporter data throughout the manuscript.

claim: No cases were found of neurons using more than one neurotransmitter.
source: We did not find any cases of neurons using more than one neurotransmitter, but found that the acetylcholine specific gene ChAT is transcribed in many glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, but these transcripts typically do not leave the nucleus and are not translated.
evidence: This is supported by mutually exclusive expression patterns of neurotransmitter markers and antibody staining data.

claim: The ChAT gene is transcribed in many glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons.
source: We did not find any cases of neurons using more than one neurotransmitter, but found that the acetylcholine specific gene ChAT is transcribed in many glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, but these transcripts typically do not leave the nucleus and are not translated.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA in situ hybridization showing ChAT transcripts in non-cholinergic neurons.

claim: ChAT transcripts in glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons typically do not leave the nucleus and are not translated.
source: We did not find any cases of neurons using more than one neurotransmitter, but found that the acetylcholine specific gene ChAT is transcribed in many glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, but these transcripts typically do not leave the nucleus and are not translated.
evidence: This is supported by RNA in situ hybridization showing nuclear localization of ChAT transcripts and absence of ChAT protein in these cells.

claim: All neurons within a hemilineage use the same neurotransmitter.
source: Importantly, our work uncovered a simple rule: All neurons within a hemilineage use the same neurotransmitter.
evidence: This is the central finding of the study, supported by comprehensive mapping of all 34 hemilineages.

claim: Neurotransmitter identity is acquired at the stem cell level.
source: Thus, neurotransmitter identity is acquired at the stem cell level.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that all neurons within a hemilineage (derived from the same neuroblast) use the same neurotransmitter.

claim: The ventral nerve cord of Drosophila melanogaster is home to circuits coding for vital behaviors such as walking, jumping, and flight.
source: The ventral nerve cord (VNC) of Drosophila melanogaster is home to circuits coding for vital behaviors, such as walking, jumping, and flight (Harris et al., 2015; Gowda et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The VNC is composed of about 16,000 neurons.
source: It is composed of about 16,000 neurons, all of which arise from a set of segmentally repeated 30 paired and one unpaired neural stem cells (Neuroblasts [NBs]) (Bossing et al., 1996; Schmid et al., 1999; Lacin and Truman, 2016; Shepherd et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: All VNC neurons arise from a set of segmentally repeated 30 paired and one unpaired neural stem cells (Neuroblasts).
source: It is composed of about 16,000 neurons, all of which arise from a set of segmentally repeated 30 paired and one unpaired neural stem cells (Neuroblasts [NBs]) (Bossing et al., 1996; Schmid et al., 1999; Lacin and Truman, 2016; Shepherd et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous developmental studies.

claim: NBs generate unique progeny via undergoing two rounds of proliferation: a brief embryonic and an extended postembryonic phase.
source: NBs generate unique progeny via undergoing two rounds of proliferation: a brief embryonic and an extended postembryonic phase (Truman and Bate, 1988; Truman et al., 2004; Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous developmental studies.

claim: Embryonic neurogenesis generates the neurons of the larval CNS.
source: Embryonic neurogenesis generates the neurons of the larval CNS and many of these cells are then remodeled to function in the adult CNS (Truman, 1990; Hartenstein and Wodarz, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous developmental studies.

claim: Many embryonic-born neurons are remodeled to function in the adult CNS.
source: Embryonic neurogenesis generates the neurons of the larval CNS and many of these cells are then remodeled to function in the adult CNS (Truman, 1990; Hartenstein and Wodarz, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous developmental studies.

claim: 90-95% of the adult neurons are adult-specific and arise during the post-embryonic phase of neurogenesis.
source: 90–95% of the adult neurons, however, are adult-specific and arise during the post-embryonic phase of neurogenesis.
evidence: This is stated directly and is consistent with known developmental biology of Drosophila.

claim: The VNC contains only NBs that show a Type I pattern of proliferation.
source: The VNC contains only NBs that show a Type I pattern of proliferation (Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Each Type I NB divides repeatedly via asymmetric cell division to renew itself and to generate a ganglion mother cell (GMC).
source: Each NB divides repeatedly via asymmetric cell division to renew itself and to generate a secondary precursor cell, called a ganglion mother cell (GMC) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Each GMC divides terminally to form two neurons.
source: Each GMC, in turn, divides terminally to form two neurons, each of which acquires a unique identity due to the presence or absence of active Notch signaling (Spana and Doe, 1996; Skeath and Doe, 1998; Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The two neurons generated from each GMC acquire unique identities due to the presence or absence of active Notch signaling.
source: Each GMC, in turn, divides terminally to form two neurons, each of which acquires a unique identity due to the presence or absence of active Notch signaling (Spana and Doe, 1996; Skeath and Doe, 1998; Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on Notch signaling in neurogenesis.

claim: Within a NB progeny, the Notch-ON neurons are called the 'A' hemilineage.
source: Within a NB progeny, the Notch-ON neurons are called the 'A' hemilineage; their Notch-OFF siblings are called the 'B' hemilineage (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a definitional statement illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Notch-OFF neurons are called the 'B' hemilineage.
source: Within a NB progeny, the Notch-ON neurons are called the 'A' hemilineage; their Notch-OFF siblings are called the 'B' hemilineage (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a definitional statement illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: NBs progress through a temporal transcriptional cascade: Hunchback → Kruppel → Pdm during early embryonic phase.
source: By progressing through the temporal transcriptional cascade, Hunchback →Kruppel → Pdm, NBs generate diverse 'A' and 'B' neurons during the early embryonic phase (Figure 1B), (Kambadur et al., 1998; Isshiki et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NBs generate diverse 'A' and 'B' neurons during the early embryonic phase.
source: By progressing through the temporal transcriptional cascade, Hunchback →Kruppel → Pdm, NBs generate diverse 'A' and 'B' neurons during the early embryonic phase (Figure 1B), (Kambadur et al., 1998; Isshiki et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations and Figure 1B.

claim: NBs express Castor and Grainyhead in late embryonic stages.
source: Subsequently, NBs express Castor and Grainyhead in late embryonic stages and many NBs maintain this Castor/Grainyhead expression into the postembryonic stages (Almeida and Bray, 2005; Maurange et al., 2008; Lacin and Truman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Many NBs maintain Castor/Grainyhead expression into the postembryonic stages.
source: Subsequently, NBs express Castor and Grainyhead in late embryonic stages and many NBs maintain this Castor/Grainyhead expression into the postembryonic stages (Almeida and Bray, 2005; Maurange et al., 2008; Lacin and Truman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Neurons of a hemilineage born during late embryonic and early postembryonic stages often adopt similar fates.
source: Correlated with this shared gene expression, neurons of a hemilineage ('A' or' B') that are born during the late embryonic and early postembyonic stages often adopt similar fates (Truman et al., 2010; Lacin and Truman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Immature neurons of each hemilineage cluster together in the larva.
source: These studies revealed that in the larva, the immature neurons of each hemilineage cluster together and extend their initial processes as a bundle to the same region and that after metamorphosis, in the adult, they continue to be clustered and share common anatomical and functional features (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly and illustrated in Figure 1C, with citations to previous morphological studies.

claim: Immature neurons of each hemilineage extend their initial processes as a bundle to the same region.
source: These studies revealed that in the larva, the immature neurons of each hemilineage cluster together and extend their initial processes as a bundle to the same region and that after metamorphosis, in the adult, they continue to be clustered and share common anatomical and functional features (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: After metamorphosis, neurons of each hemilineage continue to be clustered in the adult.
source: These studies revealed that in the larva, the immature neurons of each hemilineage cluster together and extend their initial processes as a bundle to the same region and that after metamorphosis, in the adult, they continue to be clustered and share common anatomical and functional features (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Neurons within a hemilineage share common anatomical and functional features in the adult.
source: These studies revealed that in the larva, the immature neurons of each hemilineage cluster together and extend their initial processes as a bundle to the same region and that after metamorphosis, in the adult, they continue to be clustered and share common anatomical and functional features (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Neurons within a postembryonic hemilineage share patterns of transcription factor expression.
source: In addition to similar morphology, neurons within a postembryonic hemilineage share patterns of transcription factor expression.
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by the transcription factor mapping data presented in the study.

claim: Each hemilineage cluster can be identified with a specific combination of transcription factor expression in the larval VNC.
source: In the larval VNC, each hemilineage cluster can be identified with a specific combination of transcription factor expression (Lacin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Vertebrate homologs of many hemilineage-specific transcription factors are expressed in the spinal cord and are required for fate determination.
source: Interestingly, vertebrate homologs of many of these hemilineage-specific transcription factors are expressed in the spinal cord and are required for fate determination (Thor and Thomas, 1997; Jessell, 2000).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to vertebrate studies.

claim: In flies, the combinatorial expression of Lim3, Islet, and Nkx6 is observed uniquely in hemilineage 15B.
source: For example, in flies, the combinatorial expression of Lim3, Islet, and Nkx6 is observed uniquely in hemilineage 15B, which is composed of leg motor neurons (Lacin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Hemilineage 15B is composed of leg motor neurons.
source: For example, in flies, the combinatorial expression of Lim3, Islet, and Nkx6 is observed uniquely in hemilineage 15B, which is composed of leg motor neurons (Lacin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citation and data in the manuscript.

claim: In mice, homologs of Lim3, Islet, and Nkx6 are essential for the identity of spinal motor neurons.
source: In mice, homologs of these three factors are essential for the identity of spinal motor neurons (Tsuchida et al., 1994; Lacin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by citations to vertebrate studies.

claim: Interneurons in the vertebrate spinal cord are organized into discrete cardinal classes that share developmental origins, transcription factor and neurotransmitter expression, and functional roles.
source: Indeed, interneurons in the vertebrate spinal cord are also organized into discrete cardinal classes that share developmental origins, transcription factor and neurotransmitter expression, and functional roles (Briscoe et al., 2000; Jessell, 2000; Zhang et al., 2008; Arber, 2012; Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by multiple citations to vertebrate studies.

claim: The fly VNC is organized in an analogous manner to the vertebrate spinal cord, with developmental origins providing the basis for transcription factor expression and functional properties.
source: The fly VNC appears to be organized in an analogous manner, with the developmental origins of neuronal clusters providing the basis for their transcription factor expression and functional properties.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement based on the comparison between fly and vertebrate data.

claim: Studies on grasshoppers showed that clusters of GABAergic interneurons were based on their lineage of origin.
source: Studies on grasshoppers (Siegler et al., 2001) and Manduca sexta (Witten and Truman, 1991) showed that clusters of GABAergic interneurons were based on their lineage of origin.

source: gad1 and ChAT encode enzymes that are required for the production of GABA and acetylcholine, respectively, while VGlut encodes a glutamate transporter (Slemmon et al., 1991; Kulkarni et al., 1994; Daniels et al., 2004).

source: Glutamate can serve as an inhibitory or excitatory neurotransmitter in the fly CNS depending on the neuronal type (Daniels et al., 2004; Liu and Wilson, 2013).

claim: The 14A hemilineage contains 67 ± 2 neurons (n = 5 hemisegments).
source: This split-GAL4 combination identified the 14A (67 ± 2 neurons; n = 5 hemisegments) and 21A (63 ± 1 neurons; n = 3 hemisegments) hemilineages as likely glutamatergic (Figure 3A,B).

claim: The 21A hemilineage contains 63 ± 1 neurons (n = 3 hemisegments).

claim: All 14A and 21A neurons express VGlut protein.

claim: All neurons within 14A and 21A hemilineages acquire a glutamatergic fate.

evidence: This is stated directly and supported by the immunohistochemistry and genetic reporter data.

claim: Motor neurons in Drosophila use glutamate as the choice of neurotransmitter for muscle excitation.

source: 15B and 24A hemilineages are made of entirely motor neurons, which innervate the leg musculature (Truman et al., 2004; Baek and Mann, 2009; Truman et al., 2010).

claim: Neither GABA nor ChAT protein was detected in 15B and 24A lineages.
source: As expected, antibodies detected vGLUT protein in the motor neurons of lineage 15B and 24A, which were visualized via NB intersected reporter immortalization (Figure 4A,B; Table 1), but neither GABA nor ChAT protein was detected in these lineages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,H).

claim: The 2A neurons innervate flight-related neuropils.
